ontology.description: Behavioral signal ontology with 11 facets and 98 signals

prosody.label: Prosody
prosody.description: Acoustic characteristics of speech independent of word choice

signals.low_pitch_variance: Pitch remains within a narrow frequency range across a turn
signals.high_pitch_variance: Noticeable pitch modulation within a turn, including rises and falls
signals.rising_terminal: Utterance ends with an upward pitch movement
signals.falling_terminal: Utterance ends with a downward pitch movement
signals.flat_intonation: Minimal pitch movement across the utterance, including terminal position
signals.speech_rate_fast: Words produced at a higher-than-baseline tempo for the speaker
signals.speech_rate_slow: Words produced at a lower-than-baseline tempo for the speaker
signals.clipped_phrasing: Syllables or words shortened or cut off abruptly
signals.elongated_vowels: Vowel sounds audibly extended beyond typical duration
signals.volume_increase: Audible rise in loudness within or across turns
signals.volume_decrease: Audible reduction in loudness within or across turns
signals.creaky_voice: Low-frequency, irregular vocal fold vibration (vocal fry)

lexical_choice.label: Lexical Choice
lexical_choice.description: Patterns in word and phrase selection

signals.hedging_terms: Use of words that soften commitment (e.g., 'maybe', 'kind of')
signals.certainty_terms: Use of words expressing confidence or finality (e.g., 'definitely', 'clearly')
signals.mitigators: Words reducing force or imposition (e.g., 'just', 'a bit')
signals.abstract_language: Use of generalized or conceptual terms rather than concrete entities
signals.concrete_language: Use of specific, tangible, or directly referable terms
signals.modal_verbs: Use of modals expressing possibility, obligation, or ability (e.g., 'might', 'should')
signals.formal_register: Structured or institutional vocabulary and syntax

turn_taking.label: Turn Taking
turn_taking.description: How conversational floor access is managed

signals.interruptions: Speaker begins while another speaker is mid-turn, cutting them off
signals.overlaps: Simultaneous speech without clear interruption intent
signals.rapid_backchannels: Short acknowledgements produced quickly after or during turns
signals.delayed_backchannels: Acknowledgements produced after a noticeable delay
signals.long_turns: Turns significantly longer than interlocutor's or speaker's baseline
signals.floor_holding: Behaviours preventing turn transfer (e.g., continued speech, fillers)
signals.floor_yielding: Clear cues inviting the other speaker to take the floor
signals.competitive_entry: Entering the floor at transition-relevant points with assertive timing
signals.smooth_transition: Turn exchanges without overlap, interruption, or delay

gaze.label: Gaze
gaze.description: Eye direction and movement relative to interlocutors

signals.gaze_aversion: Eyes oriented away from interlocutor during interaction
signals.gaze_shift_frequency_high: Frequent changes in gaze direction within a short time
signals.gaze_shift_frequency_low: Sustained gaze direction with few shifts
signals.downward_gaze: Eyes oriented downward relative to head position
signals.side_glance: Brief lateral gaze movement without head turn
signals.gaze_following: Gaze tracks another speaker's movement or focus
signals.gaze_fixation: Prolonged gaze on a single point or target

facial_expression.label: Facial Expression
facial_expression.description: Visible facial muscle movements, without inferred emotion

signals.smile: Sustained upward movement of lip corners
signals.brow_furrow: Inward or downward movement of eyebrows
signals.jaw_tension: Visible tightening or clenching of jaw muscles
signals.expression_freeze: Facial expression held unusually still across time

gesture.label: Gesture
gesture.description: Hand and arm movements accompanying interaction

signals.expansive_gesture: Broad movements extending away from the body
signals.restricted_gesture: Small or minimal hand movements close to the body
signals.illustrative_gesture: Movements that visually depict speech content
signals.beat_gesture: Rhythmic movements aligned with speech timing
signals.gesture_synchrony_high: Gestures closely aligned with speech rhythm
signals.gesture_synchrony_low: Gestures weakly or inconsistently aligned with speech

signals.backward_lean: Upper body inclined away from interlocutor
signals.upright_posture: Spine aligned vertically with minimal slouch
signals.postural_shift_frequency_low: Sustained body position with minimal movement

affect_regulation.label: Affect Regulation
affect_regulation.description: Behaviours that modulate or constrain expressive output

signals.self_soothing_touch: Repetitive touch actions (e.g., rubbing hands, neck)
signals.suppressed_expression: Visible inhibition of facial or vocal expression
signals.forced_smile: Smile not accompanied by other facial movements
signals.affect_dampening: Reduction in expressive intensity over time
signals.affect_amplification: Increase in expressive intensity over time
signals.respiratory_control_visible: Audible or visible breath control (e.g., sighs, breath holds)

signals.initiative_taking: Initiating topics or actions without prompt
signals.topic_shift: Redirecting conversation to a new topic
signals.alignment_behavior: Behaviours matching interlocutor's framing or stance

signals.response_latency_short: Minimal delay between turn completion and response
signals.pause_mid_turn: Silent pause occurring within a turn

signals.self_correction: Speaker revises their own speech content
signals.rephrasing: Same idea restated with different wording
